Derivatives of a Parameter by One Tensor Stencil per Component

Source: R/numerical_fallbacks.R
param_tensor.Rd

Computes the derivatives of order order of param_value() or, with what = "logdet", of param_logdet(), through numericals7::fd_tensor(). The analytic derivatives of lower order, as param_analytic() reads them, are declared to it, so each component is one tensor-product central difference of the highest analytic quantity below it, and of the value itself where there is none.

Usage

param_tensor(s, eta, order, what = c("value", "logdet"), accuracy = 4L)

Arguments

s

A parameter() object.

eta

A numeric vector of free values, of length s@n_free.

order

The derivative order, 1 to 4.

what

"value" or "logdet".

accuracy

The order of accuracy of the one-dimensional stencils.

Value

For "value", a list of estimates keyed as param_tuple_names(s, order) and in that order, each of which has the shape of param_value()'s result. For "logdet", a named numeric vector in the same order.

Details

The coordinates are the free values. The value is flattened to a vector, and each component is returned with the attributes of param_value()'s result and, for a matrix_parameter(), symmetrized as (m + t(m)) / 2. The step of a component whose difference is of order \(r\) is \(\varepsilon^{1/(r + a)}\max(1, |\eta_k|)\), with \(a\) the accuracy; the unconstrained scale has no bounds.

See also

numerical_d1() to numerical_d4(), param_d3logdet.matrix_parameter() and param_d4logdet.matrix_parameter(), which call this.
